articles.title: The Massive 77" LG Evo C5 4K OLED TV Drops to $1,682 With Free Delivery Ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: If you've got the budget for it, there's nothing on the market that's better than an OLED TV. And among OLED TV brands, I wouldn't recommend any over LG now that it has dropped in price for Black Friday.
body: LG's C-series OLED TV has long been one of our favorite TVs for console gaming. It's also one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. The C5 is a 2025 model with image quality nearly identical to the current generation C6. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. It's also equipped with LG's proprietary Evo panel, which is significantly brighter and offers a wider color gamut than traditional W-OLED TVs.

The C5 is equipped with modern gaming features that make it a perfect complement to current generation consoles like the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 144Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode.

articles.title: Doctor Doom Is Not a Tony Stark Variant in Avengers: Doomsday, Confirms Kevin Feige
articles.summary: Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday. When speaking with Empire Magazine, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige debunked the popular fan theory that Doctor Doom and Tony Stark have a shared connection in the multiverse.
body: “Is Steve Rogers a Johnny Storm variant?" asked Feige. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom.”

As for what Doom's whole deal is, the creative team behind the film teased what kind of energy he brings and why he is the way he is. The Russo Brothers, who are directing the film, teased that Doom has lost a child, is a "victim of trauma" and has a greater ego than Thanos. They also noted that he's a pretty terrifying presence.

"Doom is a Gothic character,” said director Joe Russo. “He says, ‘Hell answers to me,’ and he’s not kidding. He’s a very powerful character with some very dark magic, and he’s not above selling his soul to get what he wants. He’s worth being scared of.”
Robert Downey Jr. also noted that he was excited to lean into being a villain this time around, and suggested that Doom's plans have a tremendous scope to them.
points: Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday.

articles.title: Xbox Has Spent 25 Years Tracking Your Gaming Habits; Now You Can See The Damage
articles.summary: It's the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and to celebrate, you can see how much time you've spent--or wasted, according to my parents--playing games on Xbox hardware over the years.
body: It's a neat little celebratory feature, complete with a customized video and graphics that you can show off. In addition to the date you started playing on Xbox, it includes the first Xbox console you used, the first game you booted up, your total hours played, a breakdown of game genres, and more. (There are some limits on data during Xbox's early years, though.) You can try it out by signing in to your Xbox account through this link.

Other stats you can check out include the games you spent the most hours on, which ones you got a 100% Achievement rank in, and your longest streak of consecutive play days. Xbox says you can share your record online by scanning a QR code at the end of the video that plays--just in case you want to share how many hours you've sunk into Viva Piñata over the decades.

articles.title: The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 3 Resolves One of the Most Fascinating Mysteries From Middle-earth Lore
articles.summary: Rings of Power Season 3 has revealed the true identity of Ciarán Hinds’ Dark Wizard, thereby resolving one of the biggest mysteries from J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth lore.
body: Full spoilers ahead for the first four episodes of The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 3!

Prime Video has released the first four episodes of The Rings of Power Season 3, and they’re nothing if not eventful. But amid all the warring and hoarding of magical rings, there’s also a reveal that has a lot of Tolkien nerds’ heads spinning. The series has resolved what may well be the biggest lingering mystery from Tolkien’s vast Middle-earth mythology.
Read on for a full breakdown of the big reveal in Episode 3 and how it resolves a major loose end from books like The Silmarillion and Unfinished Tales of Middle-earth.

Back in Season 2, viewers were introduced to a new antagonist played by Ciarán Hinds. Known as the “Dark Wizard,” this villain reigns over the cursed land of Rhûn. Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) is desperate to put a stop to this powerful foe, lest the Dark Wizard ally himself with Sauron and create a truly unstoppable army.

articles.title: The LEGO Hogwarts Express Book Nook Gets a Massive Price Cut Ahead of Retirement
articles.summary: LEGO first revealed its first lineup of book nooks back in 2025, and now some of them are already getting pushed to retirement. The LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Express Book Nook is one such set facing the end of its lifecycle.
body: The new discount arrived alongside Walmart's first wave of Black Friday deals. This is one of the best LEGO deals we've seen so far, so you should snap it up while stock remains at this price. 50% off is the kind of LEGO Black Friday deal we're hoping for.

Although traditional book nooks are meant to be displayed between books, this Hogwarts Express build has a few different ways of being used once you put it together. You can choose to use the two sides of the set as a pair of bookends or fold them to fit neatly between books on a shelf. Both options reveal different aspects of Platform 9 and 3/4 and the train itself. As far as book nooks go, it's a bit on the smaller side with only 832 pieces included. You also get minifigures of both Harry Potter and Ron as they were in their first year at Hogwarts.

One important note is that the book nook itself is only 6.5 inches tall. This height is generally fine for most paperbacks and smaller hardcovers, but if you have taller books in your collection it might look a little bit weird. For example, the Harry Potter illustrated books are about 11 inches tall and would absolutely tower over this set on a shelf.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 14 Players Are Mourning The Loss Of The Game’s Legendary Bassist
articles.summary: The Final Fantasy 14 community is in mourning following news that Eikichi Iwai, the bassist for the game's house band, The Primals, has died at the age of 57, and is taking to the MMORPG's main hub cities to honor his legacy.
body: An "Important Announcement" post on the official FF14 website from developer Square Enix on November 11 broke the news, and stated the development team was "deeply saddened" to inform the community of Iwai's passing.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock," the statement reads. "The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 development and operations team are overcome with deep sorrow.
"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."

The Primals, composed of Iwai on bass, composer Masayoshi Soken, localization lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and band members Tetsuya Tachibana and GUNN, are behind some of FF14's most memorable tracks. Iwai's bass in particular stands out on songs like Shadowbringers' To the Edge and Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze. The band performed worldwide at various FF14 Fan Festivals, as well as at a UK rock festival, earlier this year.

articles.title: Xbox CEO’s 25th Anniversary Message Is About AI, Even If She Won’t Say It
articles.summary: As Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has shared her thoughts on where gaming is going over the next 25 years, and people are saying her message is really more about pushing AI.
body: Sharma said modern games demonstrate the "heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago." However, the costs, resources, and risks that companies need to take on have "grown just as dramatically," she said.

"As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this," she said.

Historically, to create anything at scale required immense resources, but Sharma said that's changing. Without saying AI, Sharma said it won't be long until a single person can "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

"A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982," she said.

articles.summary: It's the end of an era for Nvidia, as its founder and longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, has resigned effective immediately. The news is also expected to complicate things for Nvidia's stock price, as it has been in decline for over a month. The internet is already having a field day with Huang's departure, with hot takes and memes dominating the discourse right now. Huang's days of pulling on his signature leather jacket and hitting the stage to show off Nvidia's new hardware are now over.

What's next for Huang? Only he knows, but he'll likely retire with a pretty substantial golden handshake. As the largest shareholder in Nvidia--a company currently valued at trillions --Jensen's stock is also worth billions if he ever decides to sell.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever players in Australia and New Zealand are struggling to get sunlight, and not for the usual MMO reasons
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.
body: But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!
points: World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.

articles.title: Ex-Overwatch 2 Lead: Blizzard Execs Pushing Overwatch 2’s Reveal Were ‘Fucking Idiots’
articles.summary: Former Blizzard game director Jeff Kaplan left the company five years ago, but the studio's Overwatch fumbles are still fresh in his mind, judging by frank remarks he shared during a podcast.
body: Kaplan appeared on an episode of Gaming World Interviews, and the conversation inevitably turned to his time at Blizzard and his "really sad" departure from the company — and everything that led up to that decision.
"I never in a million years thought I would ever quit... that's how important it was to me," Kaplan said.

The early days of Overwatch were happy, Kaplan said, but things changed after the game became successful. Suddenly, executives at Blizzard and Activision started taking an active interest in its ongoing development. Once former Blizzard CEO Mike Morhaime left the company, Kaplan opined, Overwatch 's creators started to lose control of the game's direction at the hands of a "revolving door" of clueless executives.

Fans may recall that Overwatch was originally billed as a long-term, live-service shooter that would keep improving without needing a sequel. Instead, Overwatch fans found themselves in the middle of an unexplained content drought. Kaplan alleged that this sudden shift in priorities happened because the team was told they couldn't design new heroes for the game. Instead, the team had to begin work on Overwatch 2.

articles.title: As low-effort AI slop continues to flood Steam, yet more developers announce game delays caused by Valve's growing approval backlog
articles.summary: More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.
body: Earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

New turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

"We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point."

articles.title: The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
body: The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.
"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust... for the creators of this game."

Game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

"Three Leaf Clover" strips away the safety nets, needle drops, and hand-holding mechanics to throw Niko Bellic straight into unforgiving, deafening crossfire through the canyons of Chinatown and the…

It's not just about the duffel bags and balaclavas: GTA 4's intimate understanding of cinema is key.
